title: Live pinned-host verification of the fully corrected v1.2.0.0 release candidate

host.prefix_note: The first prefix /tmp/arrtags-21.13 was abandoned by the verifier mid-run: after the first publications the verifier issued 'POST /Items/{seriesId}/Refresh?MetadataRefreshMode=FullRefresh&ImageRefreshMode=FullRefresh&ReplaceAllMetadata=false' to repair its own media setup (a Jellyfin 12 series .nfo must be named tvshow.nfo, not series.nfo), after which the episode's served Primary reverted from the published badge to the local sidecar poster while the persisted artwork-state record still asserted the published identity. That is the same class of post-publication re-adoption the documented v1.2 caution (F-21.4-2 / F-21.4-5) warns about. The abandoned prefix contributes no matrix evidence; all rows are from the fresh prefix /tmp/arrtags-21.13b, on which all library, sidecar and .nfo setup completed BEFORE the first publication and no library or item refresh was ever issued afterwards. The prefix was later reused once, after this review, solely for the two-request R1 re-confirmation probe described in the notes and in F-21.13-3.

run_window_note: started_utc is the start of the verification session (artifact identity verification and the pinned-server download into /tmp/arrtags-host-dl, which began at 11:54). finished_utc is the completion of this report including the post-review R1 re-confirmation probe, which finished at 12:39Z, so it is at or after every row's evidence. The REPORTED matrix rows were all executed on the clean prefix /tmp/arrtags-21.13b and their evidence window is narrower and precisely derivable: the prefix was created at 12:06:05Z, its first host start logged at 12:06:06Z, the first ArrTags log line at 12:06:25Z, and the final clean post-uninstall restart logged 'Startup complete' at 12:21:45Z. The latest in-row timestamp quoted in any observed field is the L4 scheduled trigger at 2026-09-30T12:12:28Z, and the latest host evidence is the L8 post-uninstall restart at 12:21:45Z; both fall inside [started_utc, finished_utc]. All times are UTC and were read back from the host console logs (/tmp/arrtags-21.13b/console.log and the saved run snapshots l8-console-run1.log and l8-console-run2.log) and from the prefix's filesystem mtimes, not estimated.

matrix.description: The MB/KB byte-unit settings surface: exact byte counts persist as bytes through the elevation-gated save path, and the served settings resource exposes the per-field unit/step/precision mapping and the restart-required note text.
matrix.command: admin GET /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration -> jq '.Limits.ProviderResponseLimitBytes=1572864 | .Limits.WebhookMaxPayloadBytes=204800 | .Limits.InventoryCacheMaxBytes=1048576' -> POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration; grep -E '<ProviderResponseLimitBytes>|<WebhookMaxPayloadBytes>|<InventoryCacheMaxBytes>' /tmp/arrtags-21.13b/data/plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml; admin GET .../Configuration; curl -o page2.html 'http://127.0.0.1:8096/web/ConfigurationPage?name=ArrTags' and inspect byteLimitFields, restartRequiredFields and the *RestartNote texts
matrix.observed:
SAVE-SIDE BYTE ROUND-TRIP: the administrator GET of the configuration was filtered to set the three byte fields and POSTed to /Plugins/40322d52-5680-449f-b33e-e01836ee2f46/Configuration -> HTTP 204 with an empty body. The persisted file /tmp/arrtags-21.13b/data/plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml then carries exactly <ProviderResponseLimitBytes>1572864</ProviderResponseLimitBytes>, <WebhookMaxPayloadBytes>204800</WebhookMaxPayloadBytes> and <InventoryCacheMaxBytes>1048576</InventoryCacheMaxBytes> (1.5 MiB, 200 KiB and 1 MiB), and the subsequent administrator GET returns the identical integers {"a":1572864,"b":204800,"c":1048576}. The stored value is therefore the exact byte count and no MB/KB rescaling occurs on the save path. The save applied at runtime with no restart: the 'Loaded plugin: ArrTags 1.2.0.0' count and the 'Startup complete' count both stayed 1 across the save.
DISPLAY MAPPING IN THE SERVED RESOURCE: GET /web/ConfigurationPage?name=ArrTags (HTTP 200, 59,154 bytes) contains the byteLimitFields table with one entry per byte-denominated field, each carrying the code-owned unit/step/precision:
  ProviderResponseLimitBytes unit MB unitBytes 1048576 stepBytes 65536 precision 4
  WebhookMaxPayloadBytes    unit KB unitBytes 1024   stepBytes 1024  precision 0
  SourceArtifactLimitBytes  unit MB unitBytes 1048576 stepBytes 65536 precision 4
  DerivedArtifactLimitBytes unit MB unitBytes 1048576 stepBytes 65536 precision 4
  RenderCacheQuotaBytes     unit MB unitBytes 1048576 stepBytes 1048576 precision 0
  ArtifactStorageQuotaBytes unit MB unitBytes 1048576 stepBytes 1048576 precision 0
  InventoryCacheMaxBytes    unit MB unitBytes 1048576 stepBytes 1048576 precision 0
so the three probed fields display as 1.5 MB, 200 KB and 1 MB respectively, with per-field step multiples of 0.0625 MB, 1 KB and 1 MB and decimal precision 4, 0 and 0.
RESTART-REQUIRED NOTE TEXT AND CLASSIFICATION: the served resource also carries the restartRequiredFields table (SourceArtifactLimitBytes mixed:true, DerivedArtifactLimitBytes mixed:true, MaxImageDimensionPixels mixed:true, RenderCacheTtlMinutes mixed:false, RenderCacheQuotaBytes mixed:false, ArtifactStorageQuotaBytes mixed:false, TerminalProvenanceRetentionDays mixed:false) and the always-present static note text, observed verbatim as 'A Jellyfin server restart is required for a change to this setting to take effect. Some paths apply the change immediately.' on the mixed settings and 'A Jellyfin server restart is required for a change to this setting to take effect.' on the non-mixed ones, plus the best-effort modal reminder text 'A restart-required setting changed. A Jellyfin server restart is required for the change to take effect; the note text next to the setting states whether some paths apply the change immediately.' guarded by an availability check that fails open.
NOT EXERCISED HERE: the page's JavaScript unit conversion, off-step rejection and modal invocation are not executed, because the documented host launcher always passes --nowebclient and there is no browser client; only the served resource and the live save path were exercised (see F-21.13-4).

[FTL] 0 and ArrTags-logger [ERR] 0 across the whole prefix.
SOURCE ARTWORK BYTE-UNCHANGED: 'find /tmp/arrtags-21.13b/media -type f \( -name *.jpg -o -name *.nfo -o -name *.mp4 -o -name *.mkv -o -name *.png \) -exec sha256sum {} \;' diffed against the run-start baseline is empty; all three source poster.jpg files, the four .nfo files and the three media files are byte-identical and no folder.png or -thumb.png appeared under the media root (SaveLocalMetadata=false).
VERIFIER ERROR WORTH RECORDING (not a product defect): the first attempt to reach this row did not re-render, because the L2 row's own administrator POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration with the body {} had replaced the entire configuration with defaults, clearing the provider Enabled/BaseUrl/ApiKey values and therefore disabling reconciliation. The verifier re-applied the full configuration (providers plus Size=ExtraLarge) through the same elevation-gated path and re-ran the trigger, after which both items re-rendered as described. See F-21.13-3: the save path uses whole-object replacement semantics, so a partial or empty body clears every omitted field while still returning 204. The administrator GET does return the provider ApiKey fields (verified live; see F-21.13-3), so a GET-then-POST round-trip that carries the whole body is safe; posting an empty or partial body is what destroyed the configuration here.

matrix.goal: G9/ADR-026 (no-regression check for the task 21.11 log-subject hardening)
matrix.description: With LogVerbosity=Information, ArrTags log lines identify media by a bounded file name with an item-id fallback, never a directory or full path and never a secret, and the bounded render classification is emitted on the artwork outcome line. This row is a NO-REGRESSION check only: it confirms the corrected build still satisfies the G9 contract and did not regress, and it is NOT evidence that the specific task 21.11 findings are fixed.
matrix.command: POST LogVerbosity=Information through /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration; grep -oE '\] ArrTags\.[^:]+: .*' /tmp/arrtags-21.13b/console.log | sort -u; grep -E '\] ArrTags\.' /tmp/arrtags-21.13b/console.log | grep -cE '/tmp/|/media/|/tv/'; grep -oE 'item [^:]*' console.log | sort -u; grep -c -e "$(cat radarr.key)" -e "$(cat sonarr.key)" console.log
matrix.observed:
LogVerbosity=Information was set through the elevation-gated POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration (204), honoured immediately with no restart ('Loaded plugin: ArrTags 1.2.0.0' count 1 and 'Startup complete' count 1 across every save in this run), and the administrator GET returns LogVerbosity Information. 22 ArrTags log lines, 9 distinct, all at [INF]; ArrTags-logger [ERR] 0 and [WRN] 0 in this prefix.
BOUNDED FILE-NAME SUBJECT (ADR-026 clauses 1 and 3) - every media-bearing line identifies the item by its bare file name:
  "Artwork generation for item ArrTags Test Movie (2020).mp4 completed with Published: The derived artwork was published and committed."
  "Artwork generation for item ArrTags Test Show - S01E01.mkv completed with Published: The derived artwork was published and committed."
  "Artwork generation for item ArrTags Sparse Movie (2019).mp4 completed with RenderPassThrough (PassThroughReason=NoDisplayableValue): The render passed through; the current artwork is preserved."
The distinct subjects observed are exactly the three bare file names; no directory, drive, parent component or full path appears. A grep of all ArrTags lines for '/tmp/|/media/|/tv/|.mkv/|.mp4/' returns 0 matches, even though every one of these items lives under /tmp/arrtags-21.13b/media.
BOUNDED RENDER CLASSIFICATION (ADR-026 clause 3): the parenthesised bounded classification is emitted on the artwork-boundary outcome line, observed 4 times as " (PassThroughReason=NoDisplayableValue)" on the pass-through outcome. The Published outcomes carry no classification because the result carries none. The classification value is a bounded enum with no free text.
SECRET-FREE: the mock Radarr and Sonarr API key values occur 0 times in the whole host console log. No path, directory or provider URL appears on any ArrTags line. The 'Suppressed 1 repeated MetadataPublished ArrTags log messages.' line is the bounded repetition-suppression notice and carries no identifier.
EXPLICIT LIMIT OF THIS ROW (the task 21.11 findings are NOT proven fixed by this run): the two hardening changes in task 21.11 are the removal of non-printing Unicode scalars (UnicodeCategory Cf and friends) and the dual-separator final-component extraction (src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs ExtractFinalComponent uses Math.Max(LastIndexOf('/'), LastIndexOf('\\')) precisely because Path.GetFileName is host-platform dependent). NEITHER behaviour is reachable on this host: the pinned Jellyfin runs on Alpine/musl, so every media path in this run is POSIX-separated, and no media file name in the fixture contains a Cf scalar (or any control, format, Zl or Zp scalar). A PASS here therefore establishes only that the corrected build still emits bounded file names with no directory, no full path, no secret and the bounded classification, and that it did not regress on the POSIX/no-Cf path. It is NOT proof that a Windows-style path, a UNC path, a mixed-separator path, or a file name containing zero-width, bidi, soft-hyphen or isolate controls is handled correctly. Those cases are covered by the repository's own LogSubject unit tests, not by the live matrix. The installed ArrTags.dll is sha256 a077a63dd0c4302dc269339a651c5e07530a596611ca94d6a8c886b68bebbbc3, identical to the packaged DLL hash recorded by task 21.12, so the binary under test is the corrected one; see F-21.13-5.

matrix.description: A simultaneous outage of both providers leaves the host up, leaves every published image byte-unchanged, and emits only bounded provider-unavailable warnings with no fatal error; clearing the outage restores provider health. Unchanged metadata must not republish and changed metadata must.
matrix.command: touch 21.13fix/radarr/failure 21.13fix/sonarr/failure; curl -H "X-Api-Key: $RADARRKEY" http://127.0.0.1:7978/api/v3/system/status; curl -X POST -H '<admin>' http://127.0.0.1:8096/ScheduledTasks/Running/0e96fc3004bcd22db45dd641e63e2666; GET /System/Info/Public; GET /Items/{id}/Images/Primary vs the pre-outage baseline; then rm -f the markers, re-verify 200, re-trigger and confirm health returns to Healthy. Unchanged/changed sub-checks: a scheduled trigger with the pristine fixture, then a fixture edit giving the sparse movie a file record followed by one configuration save.
matrix.observed:
UNCHANGED METADATA DID NOT REPUBLISH: with the pristine committed fixture, a scheduled-task trigger (HTTP 204) left both owned items byte-identical - EP 20,940 / C5264213... and MOVIE 18,144 / 83A03087... before and after - each still equal to its persisted ActiveImageIdentity with State 1 and Own 0, and the artwork-state files were not rewritten.
CHANGED METADATA DID REPUBLISH: the verifier's own fixture copy was edited to give the sparse movie a file record (hasFile=true, movieFileId=12, with a 2160p/TrueHD/x265/HEVC 10-bit HDR10 file record added to moviefile.json). After ONE configuration save (HTTP 204, the post-save trigger) the sparse movie published for the first time: served 15,884 bytes / 7EF0BEB1... == persisted ActiveImageIdentity 7EF0BEB1..., State 1, Own 0, replacing the untouched 3,473-byte source poster it had been serving as a RenderPassThrough(NoDisplayableValue). CONFIRMED PROCEDURE NOTE (reproduces F-21.9-6 exactly): the scheduled trigger issued immediately after the fixture edit did NOT cover the changed item - the sparse movie was still serving the 3,473-byte source poster - and the change only became visible after the additional configuration save, because a scheduled run resumes from the persisted ADR-022 durable reconciliation cursor anchor while the post-save trigger always enumerates from the start. This is not provider-inventory-cache staleness: every reconciliation, including the scheduled one, invalidates the inventory (ADR-018 clause 3).
OUTAGE INJECTION (the documented marker mechanism, applied to the verifier's own fixture copy under /tmp/final-review/live-host/21.13fix so no committed file is touched): 'touch 21.13fix/radarr/failure 21.13fix/sonarr/failure'. The outage was confirmed at the source: with the mock Radarr key GET http://127.0.0.1:7978/api/v3/system/status -> 503, and with the mock Sonarr key GET http://127.0.0.1:9089/api/v3/system/status -> 503. The mock stayed up and logged 29 status=503 responses across the window.
TRIGGER: POST /ScheduledTasks/Running/0e96fc3004bcd22db45dd641e63e2666 -> HTTP 204. No library refresh was used, so no sidecar re-adoption occurred during this row.
HOST STAYS UP: GET /System/Info/Public returned HTTP 200 during the outage window.

findings.detail:
CORRECTED AFTER REVIEW (R3) to match the recorded evidence exactly; the substance is unchanged from F-21.4-2 and F-21.9-2 and is carried forward. What this run actually observed is narrower than an OwnershipLost transition, and is stated as such: on the abandoned prefix /tmp/arrtags-21.13 the episode's served Primary image REVERTED from the published 13,751-byte badge back to the 3,473-byte source sidecar immediately after a targeted per-item refresh, while the persisted artwork-state record continued to assert the published identity (State 1, ActiveImageIdentity 9B084736..., JellyfinImageTag 399970910952d40cb3876a7a6b7a2c49). The verifier did NOT observe and does NOT claim that the item transitioned to the OwnershipLost state on this prefix, and it did not inspect the ownership-observation counter after the revert. This is the documented fail-closed divergence shape that the v1.2 caution warns about - the host-adopted image no longer matching the plugin's recorded active identity - and it is the same class of condition that F-21.4-2 characterises as OwnershipLost, but this run does not add independent evidence for that transition and makes no claim about it.
This was not a reproduction attempt against the release candidate. The verifier hit it while repairing its own media setup: on Jellyfin 12 a series .nfo must be named tvshow.nfo, and the refresh used to re-read the corrected series metadata re-adopted the local sidecar poster as the episode's Primary image. The verifier deliberately abandoned that prefix rather than clear the state out of band, because doing so would simulate an undocumented operator action rather than exercise the product. All matrix rows are therefore reported from the clean prefix /tmp/arrtags-21.13b, where all library, sidecar and .nfo setup completed before the first publication and no library or item refresh was issued afterwards; all three items stayed State 1 with LastOwnershipObservation.Status 0 through the Medium baseline, the Extra Large save, the unchanged-metadata trigger, the fixture edit, the total provider outage, the recovery and the restart.
The substantive open question is unchanged and this run adds NO new evidence for it: v1.2 exposes no in-product administrative action that returns an already-lost item to a publishable session.

The current item image tag observed afterwards was 0f52f4505c970960994aae9aaccb6483, i.e. no longer the tag the plugin had recorded. NO OwnershipLost transition was observed or claimed.

On the clean prefix /tmp/arrtags-21.13b: all three items State 1, LastOwnershipObservation.Status 0 at every observation point (Medium baseline, Extra Large, unchanged-metadata trigger, changed-fixture publication, provider outage, recovery, restart).

findings.recommended_action: Carry F-21.4-2 forward unchanged into the release limitations: record the owner-facing recovery path for a lost item, or an explicit decision that it is out of band. Do not weaken the caution in docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md: this run shows that a targeted per-item '?MetadataRefreshMode=FullRefresh&ImageRefreshMode=FullRefresh' re-adopts the sidecar and desynchronises the served image from the plugin's recorded active identity, the same class of divergence as a full POST /Library/Refresh, which is why the reported prefix completed all refreshes before the first publication.

findings.detail:
CORRECTED AFTER REVIEW (R1). An earlier draft of this finding misattributed the cause to the administrator GET omitting the provider ApiKey fields. That was wrong and is withdrawn: the plugin declares no JsonIgnore attribute anywhere under src/ArrTags/Configuration/ (ArrConnectionConfiguration.ApiKey is a plain public string property), and docs/research/jellyfin-12-architecture.md section 9.3 states that GET {pluginId}/Configuration returns configPlugin.Configuration unfiltered. The GET therefore DOES return both ApiKey fields, which is also consistent with the task 21.9 run, where an unadorned 'admin GET | jq .Renderer.Size=... | POST' round-trip re-rendered both items with no key re-injection.
THE ACTUAL CAUSE is the save semantics: POST {pluginId}/Configuration deserializes the request body into a fresh configuration object and BasePlugin<TConfigurationType>.UpdateConfiguration assigns Configuration = (TConfigurationType)configuration and persists it. It is a WHOLE-OBJECT REPLACEMENT, not a patch or a merge. Any field omitted from the body is therefore reset to its default. A partial or empty body silently clears every omitted setting - including Sonarr.Enabled, Radarr.Enabled, both BaseUrls and both ApiKeys - while the endpoint still returns 204 with no warning and no activity-log entry.
This bit the verifier in this run. While measuring row L2 it issued the documented administrator POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration with the body {} to establish the 204-on-save half of the elevation check. That is a real configuration write, not a probe, and it reset the entire configuration to defaults. Reconciliation stopped working as a result, and the next save (the L4 Extra Large save) applied the size change but produced no re-render at all, which looked like an Extra Large failure until the cause was traced. The row only produced its expected result once the verifier re-supplied the provider Enabled/BaseUrl/ApiKey fields in the same POST.
THE GENUINE PROCEDURE CAUTION is narrower and much simpler than the withdrawn version: never POST a partial or empty body to this endpoint. Always POST a COMPLETE configuration body. A 'admin GET, modify one field, POST the result' round-trip is SAFE, because the GET includes the ApiKey fields; the danger is hand-writing a body that omits fields, or posting {} as an innocuous-looking probe. Because the destructive request returns 204 and looks exactly like a successful targeted save, the failure is silent and its symptom (no re-render) points at the wrong subsystem.
Scope: this is the documented host/plugin configuration-model behaviour, not a Jellyfin host defect and not a defect in the ArrTags settings page. The settings page does not have the problem because it reads the whole configuration through ApiClient.getPluginConfiguration and writes back the whole object, using dedicated password inputs so the secret fields are carried through untouched.
evidence: RE-CONFIRMED LIVE after the review correction, on the disposable prefix /tmp/arrtags-21.13 where the plugin was still installed with valid provider keys persisted: 'admin GET /Plugins/40322d52-5680-449f-b33e-e01836ee2f46/Configuration' returned {"sonarrEnabled":true,"sonarrKeyLen":48,"radarrEnabled":true,"radarrKeyLen":48,"size":"Medium"}, and the response body contained both live mock API key values (1 occurrence each). The GET demonstrably returns the secret fields, contradicting the withdrawn claim.

REPLACEMENT SEMANTICS DEMONSTRATED on the same disposable prefix: 'POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration' with the partial body {"Renderer":{"Size":"Large"}} returned HTTP 204, and the subsequent administrator GET returned {"sonarrEnabled":false,"sonarrKeyLen":0,"radarrEnabled":false,"radarrKeyLen":0,"size":"Large","byteLimit":8388608} - only the one supplied field took effect, while every omitted field (both providers, both keys, and the previously saved 1,572,864-byte limit that fell back to the 8,388,608-byte default) reverted to its default. No warning, no rejection and no activity-log entry accompanied the 204.

The mechanism is documented, not inferred: docs/research/jellyfin-12-architecture.md section 9.3 shows POST {pluginId}/Configuration deserializing Request.Body to ConfigurationType and calling UpdateConfiguration, and BasePlugin.UpdateConfiguration as 'Configuration = (TConfigurationType)configuration; SaveConfiguration(Configuration);'. A grep for JsonIgnore under src/ArrTags/Configuration/ returns nothing.

The in-run instance of the same behaviour: after the L2 administrator 'POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration -d {}' (HTTP 204) the administrator GET returned {"size":"ExtraLarge","pos":"BottomLeft","lv":"Warning","s":false,"r":false,"keylens":[0,0]} - both providers disabled and both API keys empty - while the same endpoint had returned enabled providers with 48-character keys immediately before.

The subsequent L4 Extra Large save returned 204 and persisted <Size>ExtraLarge</Size>, but two reconciliation triggers produced no new artwork identity at all and no 'Artwork generation ... completed with' line appeared for either badge item; the console still showed only configuration v2 activity.

After re-supplying .Sonarr.Enabled/.Sonarr.BaseUrl/.Sonarr.ApiKey and .Radarr.Enabled/.Radarr.BaseUrl/.Radarr.ApiKey in the same POST (HTTP 204), the very next scheduled trigger published both items at Extra Large (MOVIE 13,219 -> 18,144, EP 13,751 -> 20,940), proving the size setting itself was never the problem.
findings.recommended_action: Record the trap in docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md alongside the F-21.9-6 note: POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration replaces the entire configuration, so always POST a complete body and never an empty or partial one; a 'admin GET, edit one field, POST it back' round-trip is safe because the GET includes the provider ApiKey fields. Do not use an empty-body POST as a non-destructive way to test the 204 save path - it silently resets the configuration. Whether the plugin should instead warn or reject a save that disables every provider while the previous configuration enabled one is a product decision and is out of scope for this verification.

findings.detail: Unchanged residuals, recorded again for this run. (1) Uninstall residue, identical to F-21.4-6 and F-21.9-5: after DELETE /Plugins/{guid}/1.2.0.0 returned 204 the versioned install folder and the relocated state root were both removed and the drain restored the original source artwork, but the host-owned data/plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml survived with the last saved configuration, and the already-loaded ArrTagsStatusController continued to answer administrator GET /ArrTags/Status with 200 (still 401 for anonymous) until the next restart, after which it returns 404. This is an observation, not a defect, but any release documentation claiming a fully clean uninstall must carry the qualifier. (2) Non-executable surfaces, identical to F-21.4-4 and F-21.9-4 and to the residuals already registered in docs/limitations/00-index.md (V12-G6-1, V12-G8-1, V12-G8-2): the settings page's JavaScript unit conversion, off-step rejection and modal reminder, and the diagnostics panel's unauthorized behaviour, were verified only against the served resource and the live endpoints, not by running their code, because the documented host launcher always passes --nowebclient and there is no browser client; and the Extra Large safe-area clamp / shorten-omit path for over-long badge text and the Extra Large golden images require a JavaScript-capable client or a unit-level render assertion. The task 21.7 redirect-transport hardening (SEC-21.5-01) is likewise unobservable here because the committed mock fixture answers plain HTTP 200 without redirects; that path is covered by the repository's ProviderRedirectTransportTests.
evidence: 5-8 s after the DELETE: /tmp/arrtags-21.13b/data/plugins/ArrTags_1.2.0.0 absent, /tmp/arrtags-21.13b/data/ArrTags absent, data/plugins contains only 'configurations'; administrator GET /ArrTags/Status -> 200 and anonymous -> 401; /web/ConfigurationPage?name=ArrTags -> 404 and /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration -> 404.

After the following clean restart: /ArrTags/Status -> 404, /web/ConfigurationPage?name=ArrTags -> 404, /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration -> 404, GET /Plugins contains 0 ArrTags entries, and the 77-line log contains 0 occurrences of the string 'ArrTags'.

scripts/provision-jellyfin-test-host.sh always passes --nowebclient, so /web/ConfigurationPage?name=ArrTags is served as a static resource (59,154 bytes) with no client to run it; scripts/mock-arr-fixture.cs has no redirect-emitting path.
findings.recommended_action: None required; the bounds are already documented. Keep the structural/unit-test-only qualifier on any release claim about the page conversion, the panel behaviour, the Extra Large clamp path or the redirect transport, and note the configuration-XML and resident-controller residue if the release documentation claims a fully clean uninstall.

findings.detail: Row L6 passes, but it is explicitly a NO-REGRESSION check and must not be read as proof that the task 21.11 SEC-21.5-02/SEC-21.5-03 findings are fixed. The two hardening changes are the removal of non-printing Unicode scalar categories (UnicodeCategory Cf, Cc, Zl, Zp) from the file-name subject and the dual-separator final-component extraction in LogSubject.ExtractFinalComponent, which uses Math.Max(LastIndexOf('/'), LastIndexOf('\\')) precisely because Path.GetFileName is host-platform dependent. NEITHER behaviour is reachable on the pinned host: it runs Jellyfin on Alpine/musl, so every media path is POSIX-separated, and no media file name in the committed fixture contains a Cf (or any control, format, Zl or Zp) scalar. This run therefore establishes only that the corrected build still emits bounded bare file names with no directory, no full path, no secret and the bounded render classification, and that it did not regress on the POSIX, no-Cf path. It provides no live evidence for a Windows-style path, a UNC path, a mixed-separator path, or a file name containing zero-width, bidi, soft-hyphen or isolate controls. The binary under test is confirmed to be the corrected one (installed ArrTags.dll sha256 a077a63d... == task 21.12's packaged hash), so this is a coverage gap in the live matrix, not a doubt about which build was installed. The item-id fallback subject was likewise not exercised live, because every media-bearing call site in this run had a usable file name.
evidence: The live log shows only three distinct media subjects, all POSIX bare file names: 'ArrTags Test Movie (2020).mp4', 'ArrTags Test Show - S01E01.mkv' and 'ArrTags Sparse Movie (2019).mp4'; a grep of all ArrTags lines for '/tmp/|/media/|/tv/|.mkv/|.mp4/' returns 0 matches even though every item lives under /tmp/arrtags-21.13b/media.

src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs documents and implements the two hardened behaviours (ExtractFinalComponent with Math.Max over both separators; NormalizeFileName removing Cc/Cf/Zl/Zp), neither of which is observable with musl paths and ASCII file names.
sha256sum /tmp/arrtags-21.13b/data/plugins/ArrTags_1.2.0.0/ArrTags.dll -> a077a63dd0c4302dc269339a651c5e07530a596611ca94d6a8c886b68bebbbc3, the packaged hash recorded by task 21.12.
findings.recommended_action: State the limitation explicitly wherever the corrected 1.2.0.0 candidate is certified: the SEC-21.5-02/SEC-21.5-03 log-subject findings are established by the repository's LogSubject unit tests and not by the pinned-host live matrix, which cannot produce a Windows-style, UNC, mixed-separator or Cf-bearing media path. If a live demonstration is wanted, it needs a host or fixture that can present such a path, which the current pinned-musl procedure cannot.

notes: SCOPE. This is the Phase 21 corrective re-run of the v1.2 pinned-host end-to-end matrix against the FULLY CORRECTED 1.2.0.0 release candidate produced by task 21.12 after the task 21.11 SEC-21.5-02/SEC-21.5-03 log-subject fix, which itself followed the task 21.7 SEC-21.5-01 transport fix. It supersedes the task 21.9 run (3e59cb06.../619,636) and the task 21.4 run (50580499.../619,538). Neither docs/implementation/21.9/live-verification.json nor docs/implementation/21.4/live-verification.json was modified; both remain the historical record of their own artifacts.

ARTIFACT IDENTITY was verified before install and is unmodified on disk: 619,861 bytes, SHA-256 2a039fc7075f4e4c1a1c785eb0b3757636fc0573da1361ee814cfd4099297268, MD5 631fbfa5a4fb58fac5a877eeef761193, 7 entries. It equals docs/release/build-and-release.md 'Release artifact identity' for 1.2.0.0 and manifest.json versions[0].checksum. The archive was extracted read-only into the versioned install folder. No product file, test, canonical document, PLANS.md, docs/plan/state.json, manifest.json, artifact, or prior verification report was modified, and no commit or tag was created.

HOST. All rows were executed on /tmp/arrtags-21.13b, provisioned with the documented script 'scripts/provision-jellyfin-test-host.sh'. The pinned server archive was downloaded once into /tmp/arrtags-host-dl/jellyfin_12.0.tar.gz (119,083,810 bytes, exactly the documented size), extracted into the prefix before invoking the script so the ~119 MB fetch was skipped, and the script then fetched and extracted the Alpine runtime packages exactly as documented. Console confirms 'Main: Jellyfin version: 12.0.0' (amd64-musl, self-contained). The first prefix /tmp/arrtags-21.13 was abandoned by the verifier for the reason recorded in F-21.13-2 and in the host.prefix_note field; it contributed no matrix evidence.

PROVIDER FIXTURE. The committed scripts/mock-arr-fixture.cs was run against a copy of scripts/mock-arr-fixtures placed under the verifier's own directory (/tmp/final-review/live-host/21.13fix) on ports 7978 (radarr) and 9089 (sonarr), so the outage marker files and the edited radarr records never touched a committed file. Randomly generated 48-character API keys were passed via ARRTAGS_MOCK_RADARR_KEY/ARRTAGS_MOCK_SONARR_KEY, are recorded neither in the repository nor in this report, and appear 0 times in the host console log and 0 times in the diagnostics body. The mock logs only apiKey=valid / apiKey=missing-unenforced, never a key value.

CONFIGURATION. The plugin was configured exclusively through the elevation-gated POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration path. ArrTags.xml was never hand-written; the L3 evidence shows the byte values arriving through the API save and appearing in the persisted XML. See F-21.13-3 for the whole-object replacement semantics of that save path and the procedure caution that follows from it: always POST a complete configuration body, never a partial or empty one. A GET-then-POST round-trip that carries the whole body is safe because the administrator GET does return the provider ApiKey fields.

LIBRARY AND SIDECAR SETUP COMPLETED BEFORE THE FIRST PUBLICATION. Libraries were added with EnableInternetProviders=false and SaveLocalMetadata=false as the documented procedure requires, which is what makes the source-preservation observation meaningful. All .nfo files were in place before the libraries were added, and the only refreshes were the two 'refreshLibrary=true' library adds themselves. No POST /Library/Refresh and no POST /Items/{id}/Refresh was issued at any point after the first publication on this prefix, and every later re-render was driven by POST /ScheduledTasks/Running/0e96fc3004bcd22db45dd641e63e2666. As a result no item entered OwnershipLost on the reported prefix.

ONE PROCEDURE GAP WORTH RECORDING FOR FUTURE VERIFIERS: on Jellyfin 12 a series .nfo must be named tvshow.nfo. A series.nfo with the correct uniqueid elements is silently ignored, the Series item ends up with no provider ids, and because MediaMatcher.MatchEpisode requires the parent series to match first (MediaMatcher.cs MatchEpisode returns seriesMatch.Status with SeriesNotMatchedReason when the series does not match) every episode is then recorded NotFound and never badges. The verifier discovered this the hard way on the abandoned prefix and had to abandon it when repairing the sidecar with a FullRefresh re-adopted the episode poster. The correct order is: write tvshow.nfo, add the libraries, verify the Series item carries Tvdb/Tmdb via GET /Items before enabling the plugin.
